title: Count What Follows
goal: Build a character Markov chain, then sample a passage from its transition counts.
hint: Click a token in the flow to see the counts for every token that can follow it.
notice: Character tokens make a tiny vocabulary, although the model needs a long context to look fluent.

check.modelMsg: Requirement: set the model to Markov, order 1.
check.orderMsg: Requirement: set the model to Markov, order 1.
check.selectionMsg: Requirement: click a token in the flow to inspect what follows it.

title: Extend the Context
goal: Raise the Markov order to 2 and watch the samples begin to resemble words.
hint: Because order 2 conditions on the last two tokens, there are far more contexts to count.
notice: More context means sharper predictions, although it also means more transitions to store.

check.orderMsg: Requirement: set the Markov order to 2.
check.selectionMsg: Requirement: click a token to inspect its context of two tokens.

title: Compare Tokenizers
goal: Switch to word tokens and compare the vocabulary and readability.
hint: Word tokens make a bigger vocabulary, although each transition is more meaningful.
notice: Larger token pieces usually create a larger vocabulary with fewer, cleaner transitions.

check.tokenizerMsg: Requirement: switch the tokenizer to Words.
check.selectionMsg: Requirement: click a word to inspect its transitions.

title: Add Recurrent Memory
goal: Meet the Simple RNN, a network that carries a memory vector across tokens.
hint: Because an RNN reuses one hidden state, it can remember information from earlier tokens.
notice: Because an RNN compresses earlier tokens into one learned memory vector, it does not need to store every transition.

check.modelMsg: Requirement: select the Simple RNN model.
check.stepsMsg: Requirement: press Train so that the RNN starts learning (at least 20 updates).

title: Train the RNN
goal: Understand how gradient steps reshape the RNN's memory over training.
hint: Training nudges the recurrent weights so that the memory captures useful patterns.
notice: The same backpropagation used in the Playground trains the RNN, unrolled through time.

check.modelMsg: Requirement: select the Simple RNN model.
check.stepsMsg: Requirement: keep training the RNN until it reaches at least 80 updates.

title: Compare Generated Text
goal: Generate passages and compare how each model continues the same prompt.
hint: Temperature controls randomness: a low temperature produces repetitive text, while a high temperature produces surprising text.
notice: Counting models and learned models can agree on common patterns, although they diverge on rare ones.

check.sampleMsg: Requirement: generate a passage to compare the models.

title: Masked Attention
goal: Meet Mini GPT, a model with one block of masked attention that looks back over the sequence.
hint: Attention lets every token weigh all earlier tokens directly.
notice: Attention is the mechanism behind modern language models, shown here at teaching scale.

check.modelMsg: Requirement: select the Mini GPT model.
check.stepsMsg: Requirement: train Mini GPT to at least 60 updates.

title: Embedding Directions
goal: Open the Embeddings tab, train the word vectors, and solve an analogy such as king − man + woman.
hint: The Embeddings tab retrains the model on Shakespeare with word tokens, then lets you solve analogies from its learned vectors.
notice: Directions in embedding space can capture analogies, a hallmark of learned representations.

check.analogyMsg: Requirement: open the Embeddings tab, train the word vectors, and solve an analogy.
